messages:
Sam (Support): FYI — customer hit a 400 on /v1/rerank. They sent candidates as an object instead of an array and our response is just a generic 400.

Sam (Support): Customer payload snippet below (redacted):
```json
{
  "query": "Which article is most relevant?",
  "candidates": {
    "0": { "id": "c_01", "text": "How to set up SSO" },
    "1": { "id": "c_02", "text": "Troubleshooting login errors" }
  },
  "top_k": 3
}
```

Sam (Support): Response from our API: `400 Bad Request` with body: `{ "error": "Invalid request payload" }` — not very helpful. Customer says this worked with another provider which accepts numeric-keyed objects.

Priya (CS): Ticket INC-5429 opened. Customer is blocked; they have an urgent migration window today. Any quick workaround we can give them?

Sam (Support): I asked them to flatten to an array, but they said the payload generator they use serializes maps. They want a transient workaround (transform on our side) or at least a clear error message so they can triage.

support-bot: A support ticket has been created: INC-5429 — priority P1.

Javier (Eng): I can repro — thanks for the sample. Quick questions: which model+version did they call and are they hitting hosted API or Dedicated? Also paste full headers (auth, content-type).

Sam (Support): Hosted API, model=rerank-v1, no special headers besides Authorization and Content-Type: application/json.

Liam (Eng): Reproduced locally by sending that payload — our JSON schema validator rejects object for `candidates`. Stack trace (trimmed):
```
ValidationError: candidates must be an array at /srv/api/validators/rerank.js:87
    at validatePayload (/srv/api/validators/rerank.js:87:15)
    at processRequest (/srv/api/handlers/rerank.js:34:12)
```

Liam (Eng): Short term fixes:
- We can provide a clearer 400 body: `{ "error": "Invalid field 'candidates': expected array, got object" }` (ETA: 2h)
- If we want to be lenient, we could accept object with contiguous numeric keys and coerce to array — but that risks hiding client bugs. (ETA for opt-in fallback: ~2 days)

Javier (Eng): For the customer now, recommend they run a quick transformation on their side (convert object -> array). I'll prepare the nicer error message so they know what's wrong.

Priya (CS): Can we send a sample curl transformation snippet to the customer?

Sam (Support): Pasting quick curl + jq example for customer to run server-side before sending to us:
```bash
# transform numeric-keyed object to array using jq
cat payload.json | jq '.candidates = (.candidates | to_entries | map(.value))' | curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @-
```

Sam (Support): I'll send that as a short-term workaround.

Liam (Eng): I'll open a small PR to change the validation error to be explicit and include the `expected array` message. If CS wants, we can later add an opt-in leniency flag for customers who need compatibility.

Javier (Eng): Also recommending we add this case to the SDKs' request validation — catch early in client-side.

Priya (CS): Thanks. I'll update the ticket and ask customer to try the jq snippet; ask them to share the original generator if they need help.

Sam (Support): Follow-up: customer ran the jq transform and rerank succeeded. They asked if we can add a note to docs about input shapes. I'll file a docs task.

Sam (Support): Closing loop here once PR with clearer error is out. Will post PR link. :thumbsup:
